title: Publishing images to a registry
idea: A registry stores images so other machines can pull them. The image name says where it lives: you tag it with that name, log in, and push.
points: A name is `[host/]namespace/repository:tag`; a repository holds one app's versions.
`docker login` stores credentials. Pushing needs them, and so does pulling private images.
`docker push` uploads only the layers the registry does not already have.
A tag can be moved to another image; avoid reusing version tags.

hero.title: From your machine to a server

messages.label: docker login
messages.note: Sign in once. For Docker Hub, a personal access token works in place of a password.

messages.label: docker tag
messages.note: Add the destination to the image name. This is local; nothing is uploaded yet.

messages.label: docker push
messages.note: The registry receives the layers it lacks and records the tag, for example `1.0`.

messages.label: docker pull
messages.note: On another machine, pull by the same name. A private repository needs `docker login` there too.

messages.label: layers
messages.note: The registry sends the layers, and the server starts the image with `docker run`.

code.title: Docker Hub
code.caption: Publish `bookstore-api` to Docker Hub, the default registry when a name has no host. `<docker-id>` is your username.

walk.text: Sign in to Docker Hub with your Docker ID.
Add a second name that starts with your Docker ID, the Docker Hub namespace.
Upload it. Layers the registry already has are skipped.
On any machine with access, download the image by that name.

code.title: Private registry
code.caption: A private registry works the same way, with its host name in front. Amazon ECR (chapter 10) is one.

walk.text: Log in without a prompt. `--password-stdin` keeps the token out of shell history.
Put the registry host in front of the namespace and repository.
Push to that registry. Docker Hub is not involved.

pitfalls: `docker push bookstore-api` aims at `docker.io/library`, which you cannot write to. Tag with your namespace first.
Never `COPY` secrets into an image: anyone who can pull it can read every layer.
Log in with `--password-stdin`; a `--password` flag exposes the token on the command line.

quiz.q: Which tag for the local image bookstore-api:1.0 lets you push to Docker Hub account acme?
quiz.why: A name is namespace/repository:tag, and your Docker ID is your namespace. Without one, Docker Hub assumes `library`.

takeaway: A push goes where the image name says, so name it first.
